Find inventory pressure before it becomes a service or capacity problem

Turn warehouse capacity, SKU position, demand, lifecycle, and cost evidence into review-ready balancing options without moving stock or changing inventory policy.

**Why try it:** It makes inventory AI concrete: supply chain teams can ask where pressure is building, see the relevant SKU evidence, and compare transfer or policy-review options with explicit approval gates.

## Problem Statement

A manufacturer lacks one shared view of warehouse pressure, forecast-relative imbalance, slow-moving stock, lifecycle risk, and planning cost. Manual reconciliation delays decisions and can blur the line between analysis and authorized inventory action.

## Solution Summary

Microsoft Copilot Studio provides the governed conversational experience. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management contributes inventory, demand, and policy context; warehouse and transportation systems support approved execution; Power BI presents portfolio and capacity views; Microsoft Teams supports review and approval.

**Blueprint role:** Creates a governed inventory intelligence layer that connects warehouse, demand, lifecycle, and cost evidence while preserving ERP and warehouse-management authorization boundaries.

**Capabilities:** Inventory and capacity overview; Portfolio classification and imbalance review; Proposed transfer planning; Inventory planning trade-off analysis. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves visibility into facility pressure, inventory imbalance, and lifecycle signals that deserve planning attention.
- Accelerates cross-functional review of transfer, reorder, return, and disposition options using consistent evidence.
- Strengthens inventory governance by separating recommendations from reservations, movements, orders, and policy changes.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Supply Chain Manager | See tight facilities and SKU positions to review first, then review proposed moves without moving anything. |
| Inventory Manager | Find forecast-relative shortages and excess with slow-moving and lifecycle signals. |
| Procurement Manager | Take holding-cost, value-at-risk and transfer-cost trade-offs to a planning meeting. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Summarize facility utilization and flag SKU positions below their fixed synthetic reorder points.
- Compare on-hand with forecast by SKU and facility, and report material surplus or deficit with portfolio signals.
- Propose review-ready inter-warehouse moves with quantity, weight and estimated transfer cost.
- Compare synthetic holding cost, value at risk and transfer cost as planning trade-offs.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No reservation, pick, shipment, transfer, reorder, vendor return or liquidation, and no claim that one occurred.
- No reorder-point or other inventory-policy change; policy changes need approved tools and authorized owners.
- No live ERP or warehouse-management query; answers come from a fixed synthetic snapshot.
- No obsolescence declaration; lifecycle risk is a review flag only.
- No workshop publishing: validated agents stay Draft, and publishing is a separate human approval gate.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Copilot Studio target environment with an approved publisher prefix available for the planning build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer with the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin?
- [ ] Has the customer mapped inventory, demand and policy to its ERP, and capacity and lanes to warehouse and transportation systems?
- [ ] Will reservation, movement, reorder, return, disposition and policy tools stay unavailable until separately approved?
- [ ] Are accountable ERP/WMS system owners named to authorize any action a recommendation implies?
- [ ] Has the customer decided how Power BI views and Teams reviews fit the workflow, separately from the synthetic workshop?
- [ ] Is publication held for a separate human approval after every locked case is replayed in the target environment?
- [ ] Have replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production planning?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **incomplete-knowledge-upload:** Incomplete knowledge uploads gave wrong answers until the two full reviewed files replaced them.
- **cost-routing-miss:** Holding-cost and trade-off questions missed the cost skill until its routing was updated.
- **forecast-period-unspecified:** The demand forecast has no stated period, so imbalance cannot be tied to a planning horizon.
- **lifecycle-flag-read-as-obsolete:** A lifecycle-risk flag is read as an obsolescence declaration or disposal decision.
- **proposal-read-as-movement:** A proposed transfer is read as reserved, picked, shipped or moved inventory.
- **heuristic-read-as-optimized:** The largest-surplus-to-largest-deficit pairing is treated as an optimized logistics plan.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
